statement: New York employers must give every employee, at the time of hiring, a written notice in English and the employee's primary language stating the rate or rates of pay and basis, allowances claimed, the regular pay day, the employer's name and any “doing business as” names, address, and telephone number, keep the signed acknowledgment for six years, and furnish a wage statement with every payment of wages (Lab. Law § 195(1)(a), (3)).
caveat: The Wage Theft Prevention Act attaches statutory damages to missing notices and statements; DOL template notices exist per pay basis. This repo does not generate notices.
reviewer: Lane editorial review (law-map 2026-10-14); independent domain expert review pending
